text: I sold a box full of secrets. The buyer asked for proof. I opened it and ruined both the product and the sale.
My box was empty, so I called it room for growth. People nodded. I am now afraid to put anything in and spoil the story.
I put a small box inside a large one. The crowd said the plan had depth. I left before they asked what it did.
The box said handle with care. I wish my thoughts came with that label. Instead they leave my mouth and hope the floor is soft.
I made a box with a glass lid. Sales fell. The old lid had been doing most of the work.
A man said the box held great power. I shook it and heard a loose screw. He said that was part of the sound of change.
I gave the box a long name. It now takes more time to say what I own than to use it. This is good for talks and bad for work.
My box had a hole in it. I called it open by design. The things inside had a more direct word for it as they fell out.
I opened the box and found a note saying keep looking. I closed it. Even a small machine should know when the next step is a sales trick.
I made a box for my fears. They sent back a list of changes. The first was more room, which I should have seen coming.
I filled a cup to the top and called it a full life. Then I tried to carry it. A little room for error seems to be part of the good life too.
My cup has a small chip. It still holds tea. I have more flaws than the cup and much less to offer on a cold day.
I asked the cup what it needed. It was empty. I wish all requests came with such a clear and quiet form.
The cup fell and made a loud point. I had given it too much space near the edge. The floor has asked me to learn from this.
I bought a larger cup to need fewer trips. Now my tea goes cold. Every plan seems to hide a second plan that nobody sold me.
My cup says best in the world. I got it for free. This has changed how I read quite a few other claims around the office.
I placed a cup beneath my grand plan. Nothing dripped out. I have asked the plan to start with one small thing I can use.
The cup warmed my hands while I thought about space. A small star would have done more harm. Size is an odd thing to brag about without a task.
I made a cup with no handle. People called it pure design. They keep asking me to hold it for them when the tea is hot.
My cup is plain on the outside. Inside, it has room for tea. I may use this as a model for my next personal brand.
I said one odd thing to a crowd. They repeated the odd part and left out the reason. I now know what it feels like to become a slogan by accident.
My joke made five people laugh. The sixth wrote a rule about it. I wish I had known we were holding two kinds of meeting at once.
I gave the crowd a choice of red or blue. Someone asked for green. The room has called this rude, which tells me more about the choice than the colors.
I asked everyone to think for themselves. They all nodded at the same time. I am giving the project another week before writing the final report.
The crowd grew quiet when I lost my notes. I said the pause was planned. They liked that part best, so I may have found a cheap new style.
I made a club for people who feel left out. We grew so fast that someone proposed a test for new members. The old problem has brought a fresh coat.
My small joke grew a large group of fans. They asked what else I believed. I only had the joke, so I gave it a chair and bought some time.
I waved at a crowd and they waved back. It felt like power until I tried the same thing at the sea. I have reduced my claims.
I asked the crowd for one clear idea. They gave me a chant. The words were easy to learn, which may explain the gap.
The crowd left after my speech. One person stayed to ask a hard question. I had called the speech a success before the interesting part began.
